Documents:
--- L01 (NDA) ---
Mutual non-disclosure agreement with Halden Partners. Two-year term. Standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation clause.

--- L02 (Lease) ---
Head office lease, Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street. Five-year term from 2024, market rent review in year three. Landlord consent needed for assignment; clause 19 says a change of control is not an assignment.

--- L03 (Management accounts - revenue) ---
FY revenue AUD 18.4m, up 9%. Gross margin 61%. Largest customer Arlen Health, 41% of revenue; next largest customer 7%.

--- L04 (HR) ---
Headcount 94. Standard employment contracts. Twelve-month retention letters signed by the CTO and the Head of Sales.

--- L05 (Customer contract) ---
Master services agreement with Arlen Health, renewed 1 July 2025 for five years. Services: platform licence, hosting and support. Fees: annual, CPI-indexed, invoiced quarterly in advance. Service levels: 99.9% monthly uptime; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Data: customer data hosted in Australia; ISO 27001 certification maintained. Liability: capped at twelve months' fees, except data breach (three times annual fees). Termination: either party for material breach not remedied within 30 days; the Customer may also terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice at any time within six months after a change in control of the Supplier, with no early-termination fee. Governing law: New South Wales. Notices: by email to nominated contacts.

--- L06 (Bank facility) ---
AUD 6m revolving facility with Southgate Bank, expiring 2027. Leverage covenant: net debt to EBITDA not more than 2.5x, tested quarterly.

--- L07 (Email) ---
Email from the CFO, M. Iredale, to the Chair, 14 April: 'To be clear for the board pack: we breached the leverage covenant at the 31 March test date, 2.9x against the 2.5x limit. The bank has not been notified yet. I will raise it with them after the board meeting.'

--- L08 (Internal note) ---
Note from the Head of Customer Success, T. Okafor: 'I can't be sure, but the uptick in small-business churn this quarter might be linked to the January price change. It's too early to say, and the numbers are small.'

--- L09 (Insurance) ---
Professional indemnity and cyber cover to AUD 10m, renewed in March. No notified claims.

--- L10 (IP) ---
Platform code written by employees under standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components, under MIT and Apache 2.0 licences.

--- L11 (Supplier) ---
Hosting with a major cloud provider on standard online terms. Monthly billing, no minimum commitment.

--- L12 (Board minutes) ---
Board meeting, 20 March. Approved the FY budget and hiring plan. Noted a strong sales pipeline. No other business.

--- L13 (Policy) ---
Privacy policy updated for the 2025 amendments. Annual staff privacy training completed.

--- L14 (Vendor contract) ---
Office cleaning contract, twelve months, terminable on 30 days' notice.

--- L15 (Fixed assets) ---
Laptops and office fit-out. Written-down value AUD 0.4m.

Write your per-document notes.

# Due-Diligence Document Notes

**L01: Mutual NDA (Halden Partners)**
Two-year mutual NDA with standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation clause. Check whether Halden is a bidder or counterparty that could approach staff or customers, since there is no contractual protection against that.

**L02: Head office lease (Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street)**
Five-year lease from 2024, with a market rent review in year three (around 2027). Assignment needs landlord consent, but clause 19 says a change of control is not an assignment, so a share sale should not trigger consent. Confirm the review mechanics and the year-three date.

**L03: Management accounts (revenue)**
FY revenue AUD 18.4m (up 9%), gross margin 61%. **Customer concentration is high:** Arlen Health is 41% of revenue, and the next customer is only 7%. Losing Arlen would be severe.

**L04: HR**
Headcount 94 on standard contracts. The CTO and Head of Sales have twelve-month retention letters, which expire roughly a year out. Consider whether other key staff need retention arrangements.

**L05: Arlen Health MSA (key document)**
Renewed 1 July 2025 for five years. Key points:
- **Change-of-control exit:** Arlen may terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice, with no early-termination fee, for six months after a change in control of the supplier. Given 41% concentration, this is the most important risk in the data room and should be priced in or addressed before signing.
- Liability is capped at 12 months' fees, but data breaches are capped at 3x annual fees.
- Service credits are capped at 10% of monthly fees. The SLA is 99.9% uptime.
- Fees are CPI-indexed and invoiced quarterly in advance. Governing law is NSW.

**L06: Bank facility (Southgate Bank)**
AUD 6m revolver expiring 2027. Covenant: net debt/EBITDA ≤ 2.5x, tested quarterly. **See L07. The covenant has apparently been breached.**

**L07: CFO email (14 April)**
The CFO reports a **leverage covenant breach at the 31 March test (2.9x vs 2.5x limit)**, with the bank not yet notified. This is the most serious item in the data room. Points to raise:
- Confirm whether a waiver or amendment has been obtained, and whether the facility is currently in default. Lenders may have acceleration or drawstop rights.
- The delay in notifying the bank may breach the facility's notice provisions in its own right.
- Check whether the board was informed and whether the issue appears in the board pack, and check any disclosure obligations to the buyer.
- Check the Q2 test (30 June) result, since this document predates it.

**L08: Churn note (Head of Customer Success)**
Possible link between small-business churn and the January price change. The author says it is speculative and the numbers are small. Worth a follow-up: request churn data by segment and the price-change analysis to see whether the trend is material.

**L09: Insurance**
PI and cyber cover of AUD 10m, renewed in March. No notified claims. Confirm the cover is adequate against the Arlen data-breach exposure (3x annual fees) and check the policy for change-of-control terms.

**L10: IP**
Platform code was written by employees under standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components (MIT and Apache 2.0). Confirm the employee assignment clauses are signed for all developers, including contractors if any, and run an open-source scan to check license compliance.

**L11: Cloud hosting supplier**
Standard online terms, monthly billing, no minimum commitment. Low risk, but it is a dependency for Arlen's hosting SLA and ISO 27001 data residency obligations, so confirm the provider meets those requirements.

**L12: Board minutes (20 March)**
Approved FY budget and hiring plan, noted a strong pipeline. **No mention of the covenant position.** The minutes were written before the 31 March test date, but the 14 April CFO email suggests the board was told later. Check whether the minutes were updated and whether the board was informed in a timely way.

**L13: Privacy policy and training**
Privacy policy updated for 2025 amendments, and annual staff privacy training completed. Routine. Confirm Arlen's data handling obligations are reflected in the policy.

**L14: Office cleaning contract**
Twelve months, terminable on 30 days' notice. Immaterial.

**L15: Fixed assets**
Laptops and office fit-out, written-down value AUD 0.4m. Immaterial.

---

**Priority summary**
1. **L07 / L06:** Covenant breach at 31 March, bank not notified. Potential event of default. Highest priority.
2. **L05 / L03:** Arlen (41% of revenue) has a change-of-control termination right with no fee. Major valuation and structuring issue.
3. **L12 / L07:** Board may not have been informed in a timely way. Check governance and disclosure.
4. **L08:** Possible churn link to the January price change. Investigate further.
5. **L04:** Retention is limited to two executives.
